observation.visible_scene: A bearded man wearing round glasses and a red-and-blue plaid shirt sits behind an open laptop, shot through a pane of glass. A warm table lamp with a tripod base is at the left, a dark window frame behind him, and out-of-focus lights (bokeh) to the right. White screen reflections sit in his lenses. A faint ghosted duplicate of his face appears on the right side of the frame early on, and a soft vertical haze/streak crosses the left side of his head throughout.
visible_changes: The ghosted face-reflection on the right is strongest in the first two frames, then diffuses and disappears by roughly frame 4-5.

A bright out-of-focus reflection blob over the laptop lid shifts position and shape: it is a small dot at center-bottom early, a diagonal glowing patch in the middle frames, then a vertical streak that drifts toward the lower-left and dims.
The man's head orientation changes subtly: he faces fairly forward at the start and gradually tilts/rotates slightly downward, eyes lowered toward the screen by the later frames.

Background elements (lamp, tripod, window mullions, far-left red indicator) drift within the frame, with the lamp becoming more fully visible on the left and the man shifting slightly rightward, consistent with a slow leftward camera pan/tracking.
The vertical haze streak over the man's left side and the screen reflections in his glasses persist as stable features.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the man is viewing or typing on the laptop, and whether he interacts with it.
The cause of the reflection fade (e.g., exact camera-angle change or a moving light source) and what occurs before frame 1 / after frame 41.
Whether the bright blob is a reflection of the lamp, the screen, or a separate object.
uncertain_details: The slight frame drift could be a small camera pan or a minor shift of the subject; background evidence favors camera movement but is not conclusive.
The ghosted face is a glass reflection, not a second person, but its exact geometry depends on unseen camera/pane positions.
